newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil BNDES delays Cemig debenture sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil BNDES delays Cemig debenture sale.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) said it postponed the April 25 sale of debentures convertible to Minas Gerais state power utility Cemig common shares to May 5.
The BNDES decided to delay the auction by 10 days to give interested investors more time to review information on the company, said Durval Soledad, director at BNDES Participacoes (BNDESPar).
BNDESPar is the investment wing of BNDES.

A total of 18.7 million debentures, which will be convertible to a 32.9 percent voting stake in Cemig, will be auctioned in a block sale for a minimum price of 60.37 reais per debenture to a strategic partner.
Several foreign investors have shown interest in Cemig's 33 percent stake including U.S. Southern Co, Chile's Enersis, France's EDF and U.S. AES Corp.
EDF and AES, along with other investors, hold controlling stakes in power distributor Light, which was privatized in May last year.

Brazil's Minas Gerais state, which owns a majority stake in Cemig, had previously planned to sell the shares, but scrapped its plans after the BNDES decided not to extend the deadline for repayment of a 430 million real state debt.
BNDES granted the loan in early 1996 and was issued convertible debentures. The first repayment tranche was due October 31, 1996.
As a result of the decision not to grant an extension, the shares were transferred to BNDES Participacoes (BNDESPar), which is now putting them into sale by auctioning off the debentures.
Earlier today, Minas Gerais state government sold a 3.23 percent preferred stake in Cemig for a minimum price of 46.06 reais per lot of 1,000 shares.
